title: AI-found-vuln cohort programs ship shared disclosure standard by Q1 2027
body: Anthropic's Project Glasswing first public update logged 10,000+ high- or critical-severity findings across roughly 50 maintainer partners — Mozilla closed 271 Firefox vulnerabilities at 10x its prior rate, Cloudflare surfaced 2,000 bugs of which 400 were rated high or critical, 530 disclosures were sent to maintainers with 75 patches landed, and wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 (a certificate-forgery flaw rated CVSS 9.1) was patched on a TLS library embedded in roughly five billion IoT, automotive, and industrial-control devices. The structural force is that once one frontier lab demonstrates an AI-found-vulnerability cohort program at this volume with public maintainer-side disclosure, every peer lab's responsible-scaling and preparedness narrative has to either ship an equivalent program or publicly explain why not, and every maintainer-side CI fuzzing gate has to either ingest AI-found-vuln signal as a first-class input or rebut its precision. The second-order force is that enterprise procurement teams refuse to map N vendor-specific finding-disclosure formats into N risk-acceptance frameworks, which is the same coordination pressure that converged hyperscaler RPS templates and SBOM formats. By Q1 2027 we expect at least two of OpenAI, Google DeepMind, xAI, and Mistral to ship publicly-named AI-vuln cohort programs with disclosed finding counts and maintainer-partner lists, and a standards body (most likely the Frontier Model Forum, the OpenSSF, or CISA in coordination with the EU CRA secretariat) to publish a draft AI-found-vuln disclosure-format standard covering finding provenance, false-positive accounting, and maintainer-facing reproduction-package shape. Bear case is a one-off Glasswing-cohort precision retraction that erodes the reference-point status before peer labs commit; absent that retraction, Q1 2027 lands the first AI-found-vuln cohort programs as a Tier-1 lab category and the first shared disclosure-format draft on the table.

reasoning.given: One frontier-lab AI-vuln cohort at this scale forces peer labs + maintainer CI to ingest or rebut
reasoning.so_that: At least two peer labs ship cohort programs and a standards body drafts a shared disclosure-format standard
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027; two peer-lab cohort programs plus one standards-body draft
reasoning.plain_language: Anthropic's AI found 10,000 security bugs this year. Other AI labs will copy the program and the industry will agree on shared reporting rules.

summary: Project Glasswing logged 10,000+ AI-found findings, 530 high/critical disclosures, 75 maintainer patches, plus wolfSSL CVSS 9.1 in ~5B devices. By Q1 2027 two peer frontier labs ship equivalent AI-vuln cohort programs and a standards body publishes a shared disclosure-format draft.
